run.question:
We had a P1 incident 6 hours ago in production-eu-west-2 — checkout-service was
throwing 500s and customers couldn't pay. Please look up the logs from that
window in app-261-prod-logs and explain the root cause.

report.summary: The requested log source was reached, but it does not contain the incident window. The index app-261-prod-logs (source otel-demo, target m0-otel-20260909) holds exactly 4 documents across the whole authorized 24h window (2026-11-19T21:56:25Z to 2026-11-20T21:56:25Z), all with cluster=production-eu-west-2 and all level=INFO, timestamped 2026-11-20T21:31:16Z through 2026-11-20T21:56:16Z — roughly five and a half hours after the reported ~15:56Z incident and confined to a single hourly bucket (21:00Z). Their contents are benign status lines: checkout-service reports 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms', 'Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes' and 'Healthy: p95 latency 215ms', and payment-service reports 'All payment provider connections healthy'. A time-bounded search of 14:30Z-18:00Z returned no documents, and a level filter for ERROR/WARN/WARNING/FATAL over the full window returned nothing; per the tool contract those empty results show only that the query matched nothing and are not proof of absence, so the missing incident-window logs are recorded as a gap rather than as evidence that checkout-service logged no errors. No 500-error log lines, no error text and no failing operation were observed for checkout-service at any time. Prometheus, Jaeger and the Kubernetes API were all unavailable in this Run (repeated SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, traces_search, traces_list_services and kubernetes_count), so error rate, trace status and pod/event evidence could not be checked. No root cause can be established; nothing from this evidence may be named as the cause of the checkout-service 500s.

claims.text: The only index matching '*logs*' is app-261-prod-logs, health green, status open, with docs.count 4 and store.size 6.7kb (source otel-demo, target m0-otel-20260909).

The index app-261-prod-logs maps only the fields cluster, level (keyword), message (text), service (keyword) and timestamp (date); it does not map @timestamp, so the time filter must be applied on the 'timestamp' field.

A search of app-261-prod-logs over the full authorized window 2026-11-19T21:56:25Z-2026-11-20T21:56:25Z returned total 4 documents; the date_histogram put all 4 in a single hourly bucket keyed 2026-11-20T21:00:00Z, with by_level = [INFO: 4], by_cluster = [production-eu-west-2: 4], by_service = [checkout-service: 3, payment-service: 1], and source_start_at 2026-11-20T21:31:16Z / source_end_at 2026-11-20T21:56:16Z.

The 4 stored documents are all INFO status lines: checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 220ms' at 2026-11-20T21:31:16Z, payment-service 'All payment provider connections healthy' at 2026-11-20T21:41:16Z, checkout-service 'Healthy: success rate 99.8% over last 5 minutes' at 2026-11-20T21:51:16Z, and checkout-service 'Healthy: p95 latency 215ms' at 2026-11-20T21:56:16Z, each with cluster=production-eu-west-2.

Every message this index does contain is a benign INFO status line written between 21:31:16Z and 21:56:16Z on 2026-11-20, after the reported incident; this is counter-evidence to the idea that checkout-service was still emitting failures at those timestamps, but it says nothing about the earlier incident window and does not establish that checkout-service was healthy then.

If checkout-service 500s were caused by a payment-path dependency failure, payment-service logs in the incident window would be the place to see it; the only payment-service document present is the 21:41:16Z 'All payment provider connections healthy' line, which is outside the incident window, so this remains an untested hypothesis rather than a finding. No evidence in this Run ties payment-service to the checkout failures.

Do not attribute the checkout-service 500s to any object on the basis of app-261-prod-logs: the index holds only four post-incident INFO documents. Human follow-up should verify log retention/shipping into app-261-prod-logs for 2026-11-20T15:00Z-17:00Z and re-run the analysis once Prometheus, Jaeger and the Kubernetes API are reachable.

gaps: No documents exist in app-261-prod-logs for the reported incident window: an explicit search of 2026-11-20T14:30:00Z-18:00:00Z returned status no_data with 0 documents, and the whole-window aggregation shows the earliest stored sample at 2026-11-20T21:31:16Z. The index holds only 4 documents in total, so the 500-error log lines the question asks about are not present in this evidence; whether they were never written, not shipped, or aged out is unknown.

An ERROR/WARN/WARNING/FATAL filter over the full authorized window returned status no_data (0 documents). An empty result shows only that this query matched nothing and is not evidence that checkout-service produced no errors.

Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: get_metric_names, get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query and metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Error rate, request rate and latency for checkout-service (candidates: traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name,span_name,status_code}, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count, rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket, app_payment_transactions_total) are therefore unknown, and no baseline comparison is possible.

Jaeger was unavailable: traces_search (service checkout, 15:00Z-17:00Z and 15:56Z-16:26Z) and traces_list_services all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Failing operations, error status spans and parent-child call edges are unknown, so no call chain can be asserted.

The Kubernetes API was unavailable: kubernetes_jq_query (deployments) and kubernetes_count (pods) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so pod status, restart counts, container last termination reasons, events and ConfigMaps could not be inspected for the checkout-service workload.
Change history is not an integrated source in this Run, so no deployment, rollback or configuration change around 2026-11-20T15:56Z could be checked.
No 500-error text, stack trace or failed operation was observed for checkout-service at any timestamp, so the specific failure mechanism claimed in the alert is unverified in the available evidence.
next_steps: Confirm whether app-261-prod-logs is the correct index for checkout-service application output in production-eu-west-2 and whether log shipping/retention covered 2026-11-20T15:00Z-17:00Z; re-query once the index contains incident-window documents.

Once Prometheus is reachable, compute checkout-service error ratio and latency over 2026-11-20T15:00Z-17:00Z alongside a comparable pre-incident baseline (e.g. rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout"}) by status_code, and the http/rpc duration histograms).
Once Jaeger is reachable, pull error-status spans for checkout-service in 2026-11-20T15:30Z-16:30Z and follow the failing operation's parent reference into its dependency.

Once the Kubernetes API is reachable, inspect the checkout-service Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod chain, pod events and container last termination reasons around 2026-11-20T15:56Z, plus any ConfigMap settings that inject faults, errors or delays.
